Meet airflow-ml. In the next two minutes: one raw dataset in — duplicate-checked, split-ready data out, on one platform.
One trigger starts it all: voc12_demo on a 1,000-image sample of PASCAL VOC 2012.
On the Grid, one row per run — one cell per task.
The upload job lands the sample in MinIO — images and annotations, in the standard VOC layout.
First checkpoint: verify_upload confirms every image has its annotation.
Every count lands in the task log — pairs uploaded, images verified.
Next, ingest_voc12 loads the verified sample into the dataset.
Now dedup: embed_fastdup turns each image into an embedding, then groups the near-duplicates.
Dedup publishes a report with the run — stored under the run's prefix, right next to the data.
The near-duplicate table, straight from the report.
Last step: cluster_split groups the images, then splits each cluster across train, val, and test — near-duplicates are flagged, and every split stays cluster-aware.
Five tasks, all green — raw sample in, split-ready dataset out, on one platform.
That's airflow-ml: raw dataset in, duplicate-checked and split-ready out. Bring your dataset — leave with split-ready train/val/test.
